script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 14. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

For 200,000 years, humans hunted and gathered—following food wherever it led.  Then, about 10,000 years ago, we started growing food instead of finding it.  This single change created everything: cities, writing, technology, civilization itself.

Hunter-gatherers spend most time finding food—no surplus, no specialists. Farming changed this. One farmer can feed many. Surplus food allowed some people to do other things: build, govern, create, think. Civilization grew from agricultural surplus. Farming requires staying in one place—tending crops through seasons.  Permanent settlements became villages, then cities.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Surplus creates specialization.  When basic needs are met, new possibilities emerge.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Specialization Reflection - What Would You Do?.

Here's your activity: You have a specialized skill because you don't have to find food all day. What would you do differently if you spent 8 hours daily hunting and gathering? Agricultural surplus gave you choices. What are you doing with them? This helps you appreciate how surplus enables choice.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how farming changed everything can be applied to specialization reflection - what would you do?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
